# Positive concave-array buffers: fixed-epsilon joint bad attainment

This extends the attained UNPENALIZED geometric-mean affine-multiplier setting to the full finite cone of positive concave sampled arrays. It proves positive-parameter attainment and convergence of minimum VALUES. It does not prove active-own-section properness, a stationary response payment, or OC.

The existing source `candidate 3101206ec4580190`, Section 2, already proves alignment and joint concavity for a positive real concave ell. Its parameter normalization and attainment discussion then specializes to affine ell. The new ingredients here are the exact sampled cone/extension, the zero-set arithmetic lemma, and its use to compactify ALL concave-array parameters.

## 1. The finite concavity cone and its actual extension

Let P be a finite set in its real affine span, B=conv(P). Define C(P) to be the arrays l=(l_z) satisfying

    l_q >= sum_z lambda_z l_z                              (1)

for every q in P and every lambda>=0 with sum lambda=1 and sum lambda z=q. We call such an array sampled-concave. Positivity means l_z>0 at every sample.

This is a closed polyhedral cone. For fixed q the allowed lambda form a compact polytope; a linear functional reaches its maximum at a vertex. A vertex has affinely independent support of size at most dim(B)+1, since an affine dependence on a larger support would yield a two-sided feasible variation. There are finitely many such supports and at most one barycentric representation on each. Thus finitely many inequalities suffice for (1).

Its canonical extension is the upper interpolation roof

    lhat(x)=max{sum_z lambda_z l_z:
               lambda>=0, sum lambda=1, sum lambda z=x},
               x in B.                                  (2)

The maximum is attained. Mixing representations proves that lhat is concave. At a sample q, (1) and the singleton representation give lhat(q)=l_q. Conversely existence of ANY concave extension with those sample values implies (1).

The roof is the LEAST concave function with those sample values: every other concave extension dominates every barycentric average in (2). It is continuous and piecewise affine on B. One may see this from the finite upper faces of the polytope conv{(z,l_z)}: their graphs give the roof, including their closed boundary faces. If the lifted polytope has the same affine dimension as B, all sample heights are affine and the roof is that affine function.

Two further bounds follow directly from the same feasible representation sets:

    min_z l_z <=lhat(x)<=max_z l_z,
    sup_(x in B)|lhat(x)−mhat(x)|<=max_z|l_z−m_z|.          (3)

In particular positive arrays give genuinely positive concave extensions, and convergence of arrays gives UNIFORM convergence of their extensions. There is no arbitrary interpolation choice and no loss of sampled values.

The cone has positive arrays: the constant array is one. For example, C−||z||^2 with C large is strictly sampled-concave for every nontrivial anchored representation, by the strict variance identity. Thus allowing this cone is materially more general than allowing only affine functions.

## 2. The aligned buffer and its geometric normalization

Let K_z be an actual compatible finite family of positive d-dimensional fibers, d>=1, with V_z=|K_z|, M=sum V_z, w_z=V_z/M, N=d+1. Take its canonical convex hull for real-base sections. For a positive sampled-concave l use its roof in

    f_l(z,x)=[lhat(z) E_(K_z)(x)/M]^(1/N).                 (4)

On the sampled fibers lhat(z)=l_z. Write F=E^(1/d), whose joint Minkowski concavity was proved in the ordinary energy theorem. Then

    f_l=M^(−1/N) F^(d/N) lhat^(1/N)

is jointly concave by weighted geometric-mean concavity and monotonicity. Within a fixed continuous fiber, the established identity grad E=N E a_opt gives exactly

    grad_x f_l=f_l a_opt.                                 (5)

No base differentiability of the piecewise-affine roof is required. Its one-sided affine majorants supply base supergradients whenever needed, but no new continuation theorem is asserted here.

Normalize by

    sum_z w_z log l_z=0.                                  (6)

This scale condition and sampled concavity are preserved by the actual continuous affine normalizations of the body. The sampled cone depends only on anchored representations, so it is also preserved under any of the established canonical base lifts preserving those representations.

The normalized buffered depth beta_epsilon(K,l) uses the actual within-fiber covariance norm and the through-source cap displacement epsilon f_l G_K(u). Pure-base cuts receive no displacement. Nonnegative buffering gives beta_epsilon>=beta_0.

## 3. A base center in the positive set of a nonnegative concave array

Let P be lattice-complete in its inherited affine lattice, with positive weights V_z, total M, and k occupied parities. Let h be a nonnegative sampled-concave array, not identically zero, and let

    U={z:h_z>0},       Z={z:h_z=0}.

Assume the nonstrict quotas

    V(T)<=k(T)M/k                                         (7)

for every nonempty proper closed minor T contained in Z. Then some p in U has weighted CLOSED base depth at least M/k.

Here a closed minor is P intersect conv(T)=T, and its parity count is inherited. The zero set Z itself need NOT be a face, convex, or a closed minor.

Proof. Put alpha=M/k. If every p in U has a closed containing cap of mass <alpha, choose finitely many such caps H_i={a_i z>=b_i} covering U. Choose upper thresholds U_i exceeding all a_i z and b_i. In the compact threshold box b_i<=c_i<=U_i preserve the condition that every p in U violates at least one complementary strict inequality a_i p<c_i, and maximize sum c_i.

Each nonsaturated inequality i has an equality witness p_i in U satisfying all other inequalities strictly; otherwise finiteness permits increasing c_i. The surviving strict trace T lies in Z and is closed, since its convex hull remains in the same open convex intersection. Saturated inequalities hold strictly at every base. The nonsaturated closed caps therefore cover P\T, each still with mass <alpha.

Two same-parity witnesses have an actual integer midpoint in P. Sampled concavity makes its h value positive, while their equality/strict patterns make it satisfy every complementary inequality strictly. That contradicts exclusion of U. Likewise a witness p_i and any same-parity t in T have an integer midpoint with

    h_((p_i+t)/2)>=(h_(p_i)+h_t)/2>0,

giving the same contradiction. Thus r witnesses have distinct parities disjoint from the k(T) surviving parities, so r+k(T)<=k.

The covering mass inequality is

    M−V(T)<r alpha<=(k−k(T))alpha.

For empty T this says M<M. Otherwise it gives V(T)>k(T)alpha, contradicting (7). This proves the lemma, with every closed-boundary atom retained. The inherited parity comparison is valid in lower-dimensional minors because half a difference automatically lies in their direction space. Rank zero is the single-point case.

Only midpoint concavity and nonnegativity of h were used in this arithmetic proof. This is an exact extension of the complement-face theorem, not a subtraction of all zero-set parities from all positive-set parities.

### A zero set that is not a closed minor

There is an exact seven-site calibration. Let P consist of the vertices of Delta_2 times {0}, the vertices of −Delta_2 times {2}, and p=(0,0,1). It is lattice-complete: its middle real slice is (Delta_2−Delta_2)/2, whose only integer point is zero. It occupies four parities: three paired endpoint classes and the middle class.

The array h(z)=1−|z_3−1| is sampled-concave, vanishes at all six endpoint sites and is positive only at p. Its zero set is not closed because it contains opposite pairs with midpoint p. Thus the single-face proof cannot simply be applied to that zero set.

Uniform weights satisfy EVERY strict proper-minor quota. A closed set omitting p can contain at most one point from each endpoint pair. A closed set containing p and k(T) occupied parities has at most 1+2(k(T)−1) points. Hence for k(T)=1,2,3 the maximum respective closed-set sizes are 1,3,5, strictly below 7k(T)/4; a proper four-parity set has at most six points, below seven. The point p has base depth at least four, since any containing halfspace captures p and at least one member of each opposite pair. This verifies the positive-set conclusion directly while retaining the genuinely nonclosed zero set.

## 4. Parameter escape for varying bodies

Work in a fixed compact positive body family with M=1, every V_z>=v>0, and every fiber contained in R times the Euclidean unit ball. Suppose K_j converges within this family, l_j is positive sampled-concave, and (6) holds with the corresponding varying weights w_jz.

Set

    A_j=sum_z w_jz l_jz,
    h_jz=l_jz/A_j.

The arrays h_j remain sampled-concave and have weighted arithmetic mean one. Their values lie in (0,1/v]. After a subsequence they converge to a nonnegative sampled-concave h with sum_z w_z h_z=1. The roofs converge uniformly by (3).

The normalization identity is exact:

    l_jz=h_jz / prod_t h_jt^(w_jt).                       (8)

If every h_z is positive, (8) converges to a finite strictly positive normalized array. If at least one h_z is zero, the denominator tends to zero: that coordinate's logarithm tends to minus infinity with weight at least v, while all other logarithms are bounded above. Consequently

    l_jp→infinity for EVERY p with h_p>0.                  (9)

These are all failures of positive finite parameter compactness. Unlike the affine case, the zero set can consist of several different faces; Section 3 was designed precisely to avoid presuming one exposed zero face.

## 5. Fixed-epsilon joint unpenalized bad attainment

Use exactly the original bad-sublevel compactness hypotheses of `candidate f7c05b2c30c8cfcb` and Sections 1–4 of `candidate 108870e8f9aac2e9`.

More explicitly, fix d>=1 and an original cardinality-minimal bad canonical base P. Set tau=Gamma_d/k(P), and choose b<tau above an original bad reference value. The already proved original compactness/normalization theorem supplies one compact representative family A for the whole original sublevel beta_0<=b, with M=1, V_z>=v>0 and K_z contained in R Ball. Every limiting family satisfies

    V(T)<=b k(T)/Gamma_d<k(T)/k(P)                         (10)

for every proper closed minor. This follows by restricting to that minor and applying original minimality, with the established canonical parity transfer. No new attainment of original bodies or unrestricted finite-base Helly claim is being presumed.

Fix epsilon>0. Consider a sequence of positive concave-array pairs with beta_epsilon<=b. Since beta_0<=beta_epsilon, its bodies compactify in A. If its multipliers escaped, Section 4 would give a nonnegative concave h and divergence on U={h>0}. Apply Section 3 to the LIMITING positive weights using (10). It yields a fixed p in U with limiting base depth at least 1/k(P).

At the actual centroid g_jp of K_jp, E_jp(g_jp)=V_jp>=v. The covariance minimum sigma_j=min_(||u||=1)G_j(u) stays uniformly positive on A. Therefore (9), at this fixed epsilon, eventually gives

    epsilon [l_jp V_jp]^(1/N) sigma_j >=2R.                (11)

For every Euclidean unit continuous normal and every base tilt, all fibers with nonnegative base drift from p are then wholly captured, since X and g_jp are both in R Ball. Those bases constitute a containing closed pure-base halfspace. Pure-base cuts themselves are allowed, so the buffered depth at (p,g_jp) is exactly its base depth. This is also a consequence of the independently proved whole-own-fiber capture lemma.

There are only finitely many base halfspace traces, so base depths vary continuously with the finite weights. It follows that

    liminf beta_epsilon(K_j,l_j)>=1/k(P)>b,

contradiction. Thus every bad-sublevel sequence has a positive finite multiplier subsequence limit.

Uniform array convergence, (3), positive-fiber energy continuity and covariance continuity permit the same all-direction slab comparison used in the affine attainment source. It gives continuity of beta_epsilon at that limit. Hence the full concave-array bad sublevel is compact modulo the permitted actual affine body maps, for this FIXED epsilon.

Whenever a reference pair has value <b, the infimum over ALL positive compatible bodies on this base and ALL positive sampled-concave normalized arrays is attained, with every fiber and every multiplier value positive. For all sufficiently small epsilon, the reference array l=1 supplies such a pair.

## 6. Minimum values and the exact scope of the extension

Let beta_0^* be the original fixed-base infimum. The same reference-array argument gives

    beta_0^* <= inf_(K,l in C(P), l>0) beta_epsilon(K,l)
                    <=beta_0^*+epsilon L R,              (12)

with the existing uniform slab constant L in the normalized body family. Thus the new minimum VALUES converge to the original minimum. Positivity and attainment hold at each fixed epsilon.

This theorem neither bounds l uniformly as epsilon tends to zero nor establishes proper own cuts at its optimizers. The affine subclass already has exact strict-quota escape calibrations; those calibrations are not asserted to stay optimal after enlarging the class to all concave arrays. All supporting-cap and pure-base statuses remain to be checked separately before applying a particular response calculus.

No Gamma_d/k response payment or mass-exhaustion theorem is obtained here. The enlargement is an attained extremal setting with additional legal parameter directions and a precise arithmetic compactness proof.

Supplementary exact verification: `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_concave_array_geometric_attainment_two_sided.py` passes 466 checks, including all 89 proper closed minors of that seven-site base, sampled roof equalities, the strict variance identity, and geometric-normalization escape. The compactness/attainment claims follow from the proofs above, not from these finite tests.
